utterances.text: But you are unable to say it was this type with a load of a thousand kilogrammes of explosives or you don't have further details apart from observing what you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the names, to be fair, I'm not familiar with them. I don't know the exact names of those bombs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Groome, I -- we are already five minutes past the time and I haven't apologised yet or -- even for going that far. How much time would you need because I don't want to further rely on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's just two things I want to ask the witness about. I just want to ask his basis of knowledge that depleted uranium was dropped on Sarajevo, that was one question. And the other question I was simply going to ask him, he indicated in response to a question you put, Your Honour, that he knew that there was a mortar located near the place of the incident. So I have a blank map of Hrasnica I was going to simply ask him to mark. He seems to know where the incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that usually takes at least, the two together, five minutes. I'm looking at the interpreters whether -- I can imagine that they have other things to do at this moment, so without an explicit "yes," I would adjourn for the day. Could I hear from one of the booths.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We prefer to finish for the day, Your Honour, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The English booth suggests that we finish for the day, so under those circumstances, unless I hear from the other booths, I don't see any signals, you may proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, you've just given evidence that NATO dropped depleted uranium on Sarajevo. What's the basis of that knowledge? As briefly as you can say.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basis of my knowledge is the research carried out by expert personnel from our armed forces as well as some experts from Belgrade who deal with that issue. There was a lot of morbidity --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and people are still dying today, some of whom include my cousins, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could we please call up 65 ter 09821 and could we focus in the lower left quadrant of that map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that. Mr. Ivetic, I think once the witness has been released, if it would be of any assistance to give further details of the sources the witness relies upon as scientific research on the type of bombs used by NATO, then I take it that you would be willing to assist Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will definitely talk with the witness after he has been released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we can just go down to the left lower portion of this map. I think we're a little bit high. Okay, that would be very good. If we can just focus in or zoom in on that settlement we see near the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mijatovic, this is a map of Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And again, if we could zoom in a little bit more so we can see individual buildings. And if we can go further, further. Okay, that should be good.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can we go down just a tiny bit more -- no, the other way, please. That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree that this is a map of Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the record recorded you saying in response to a question from Judge Orie: "There was a mortar near the place of the incident, so that's three." Can I ask you once again now for the last time to take the blue pen - and if the usher would assist - can I ask you to mark the place of this mortar which also happens to be the place of the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least near to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could the microphone be adjusted so as the witness says something that the interpreters can hear it. Yes, would you just mark the location of that 120-millimetre mortar you spoke about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks] [Interpretation] As far as I recall, it could be around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I would just ask that that be tendered as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 9821 as marked by the witness receives number P6533, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you have used 65 ter 15896, I think it was a sitrep report. You didn't tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I read the relevant portion, but I'm happy if the Chamber would be assisted by that as having it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's just to avoid that something at a later stage is missing --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: An oversight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on oversight.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It wasn't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Ivetic, no further questions triggered by --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Mijatovic, I would like to thank you for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to salute the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you are not here to salute. You appear here as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the instructions have been conveyed to the Victims and Witnesses Section, but witnesses may not always fully understand. First of all, I'd like to thank very much the flexibility from all those who are assisting us. As you may have noticed, I would have stopped if -- because I'm aware that everyone has his own duties on from the time scheduled for these hearings. We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 27th of May, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 27th day of May, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.27 p.m.,
